newsitem.title: GERMANY: Oil World sees higher nearby Indian vegoil imports.
newsitem.headline: Oil World sees higher nearby Indian vegoil imports.

text.p: Indian vegetable oil imports in Oct/Jan 1996/97 are estimated at 557,000 tonnes, up 22 percent from the same 95/96 period, the Oil World newsletter said.
The independent publication cited lower than expected domestic crops and high demand.

Within the Oct/Jan import total, palm oil was seen accounting for 427,000 tonnes (373,000 tonnes in the same 95/96 period), sun oil for 104,000 (11,000), soy oil for 10,000 (40,000) and rape oil for nil (17,000 previously).
Attractive sun oil prices had resulted in recent Indian purchases in the U.S. and Argentina, Oil World noted.

Four ships were due to discharge purchases totalling 75,000 tonnes in January alone and Oil World had received information another 175,000 tonnes may be received from those two countries in the next few months.
Oil World also supplied an Indian import forecast for 17 oils and fats for the full Oct/Sept 1996/97 season in a 1.30-1.40 million tonnes range versus 1.43 million in 95/96.
The figures hinged on stocks developments and the pace of domestic consumption. Indian soybean crushers were also pressing for more bean imports to be able to export more meal.
